translation: The man had built a house. Then his son came, and the son saw the house. The father said, “Now I have built the house.” The son said that he intended to travel. When the son departed, the father then sat in the house. Then the son came, and he gave his father food.
analysis: The house building precedes the son’s first arrival.
The direct-speech ic refers to the father.
The intention clause does not itself assert a journey; gewāt in the next sentence supplies an actual departure.
The last hē refers to the returning son, who gives food; his fæder is dative recipient.
On ðǣm hūse is the prior dative location.
Wolde is a reported intention, not a mechanically substituted English future auxiliary.
